mstts:express-as.prosody: Imagine walking into a workplace where everyone—no matter their role—shares in the company’s heartbeat. Where knowledge isn’t locked away in corner offices, but flows freely for all to see. That’s the world Jack Stack invites us into, with his book, The Great Game of Business: Unlocking the Power and Profitability of Open-Book Management. It’s not just about numbers on a spreadsheet or profit margins. It’s about empowering people, breaking down old barriers, and building a culture where everyone feels like an owner. What if every single person in your organization could read the financial playbook, set bold goals, and actually celebrate wins together? As we explore these principles of open-book management, you’ll start to see how collaboration and accountability come alive in unexpected ways. Teams grow closer, silos start to disappear, and a new sense of purpose takes root. Suddenly, work isn’t just a job—it’s a game where everyone has a stake in the outcome, and where the rewards are shared across the board. Together, we’ll discover how trust, transparency, and a little creativity can turn any business into a place where people thrive, and profits follow. So, let’s dive in and see just how powerful it can be when we all play the great game of business—side by side.
